page: Amazon Web Services c5n.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor with 16 vCPUs, consisting of 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance is equipped with 42.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 2.62 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

This instance type is optimized for network and EBS performance, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. The underlying Intel Xeon CPU supports Advanced Vector Extensions, including AVX and AVX-512F, along with cryptography acceleration via AES instructions. However, it lacks newer instruction sets such as AVX-512 VNNI, AVX VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and AMX extensions.

Performance benchmarks show a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is categorized as weak, placing in the bottom 25% with a score of 1407.28. Conversely, multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14808.85 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7317.0. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 89.55 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 45.22 GB/sec for writes.

The c5n.4xlarge is suited for workloads that benefit from high network throughput and multi-threaded compute, such as static web serving and Redis operations. It can handle light LLM inference, processing 148.1 tokens/sec for a 135M model, but performance drops to a weak 24.09 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a 7B model. Given the lack of local storage and moderate single-core performance, it offers a balanced cost-to-performance ratio for network-bound, multi-threaded compute tasks rather than single-threaded or storage-heavy databases.
description: The Amazon Web Services c5n.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz with 16 vCPUs, 8 physical cores, and 42.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Designed for network-heavy workloads, it provides a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14808.85, alongside weak single-core performance. Memory bandwidth is moderate, reaching 89.55 GB/sec for large-block reads. This instance is suited for network-bound applications, multi-threaded processing, static web serving, and Redis deployments, though it is less efficient for single-threaded tasks or large-scale language model inference.
